Registering on an unresolved external Future does not itself call reportSchedule in BaseActor.sendAsync. Castor's callback executor accounts work when submitted, so inactivity before input completion does not establish delivery. claims.rule: For a Castor cross-platform Context refactor, identify the members whose signatures or implementations need JVM types, isolate those members in the selected platform source set, and preserve shared dispatch and token bookkeeping instead of copying whole Context implementations. Verify that each platform gets exactly one matching mixin definition and a usable async entry point.
claims.applicability: Direct guidance from PR #12, with the concrete checking procedure inferred from its final patch. Applies to Castor's Future/ExecutionContext architecture and historical platform splits, not a mandate to introduce effects, Ox actors or a new library architecture. Recheck type availability and linker behavior for the actual current platform versions.
claims.counterexample: A JVM-only scheduling implementation may legitimately use java.time and Executors. A dead import alone is not evidence of the historical public-trait linkage failure, and the retained blocking TestBase helper is not automatically made portable by the mixin split.

claims.rule: Before calling a platform-mixin move compatible, check both old source callers and already-compiled consumers. Record the previous artifact baseline and every skipped MiMa platform/version cell; if the binary shape changes, make the release decision explicit rather than describing source compatibility as binary compatibility.
claims.applicability: The separate source/binary decision is explicit in the 2021 exchange; old-consumer checks and matrix reporting are an inference for actionable review. The 2022 Scala 3 and 2024 Native exclusions are historical observations, not excuses to disable checks on a new target.
claims.counterexample: A deliberate new-release compatibility break with a recorded migration and baseline analysis is not automatically a defect. Conversely, a private[castor] mixin can affect public inherited members and does not itself guarantee ABI stability.

claims.rule: Inference: when changing Castor's cross-module shape, verify resolved source roots, nonempty artifacts, platform-appropriate test inheritance and actual test task execution separately. Discover selectors from the pinned build and CI; do not interpret a successful artifact task or an empty MiMa baseline as a passed test matrix.
claims.applicability: Historical inference from PR #3's source-root/test repair, PR #10's missing all repair, and actual builds. The 2022 CI command is ./mill -i all __.publishArtifacts __.test; binary checks are separate. No assertion that a historical selector remains valid under a new Mill version, and no upstream command was executed here.
claims.counterexample: The shared async test is a legitimate linking smoke test despite lacking a message-delivery assertion. It should not be rejected for not being a JVM filesystem/timer integration test; it should simply not be used as evidence for stronger delivery guarantees.

claims.rule: Inference: when reviewing a portable scheduleMsg proposal, enumerate callable capabilities on each target and compare JVM parameter types before and after. A Native NotImplementedError stub is not functional support; replacing java.time.Duration with Scala Duration is not the additive compatibility proposal discussed earlier.
claims.applicability: Derived from comparing the merged #12 boundary with unmerged #15 code. This is an evidence-based review case, not a claim that maintainers rejected #15 for these reasons. Current timer primitives and duration conversions need their own version-specific verification.
claims.counterexample: A documented target-specific API may intentionally omit scheduling on JS/Native. A planned incompatible release may intentionally replace the duration type, provided old callers and the unsupported-target behavior are reported rather than silently claimed compatible.

claims.rule: Inference: while moving platform code, preserve per-message completion reporting and the scheduled-queue handoff in the unchanged shared actor engine. Separate a smoke test proving linkability from a test that observes exactly one delivery, failure reporting and eventual quiescence under accepting executors and nonthrowing hooks. Distinguish message tokens from executor/Future tokens, and do not infer external-Future completion from temporary inactivity.
claims.applicability: Source-only preservation obligation for Castor's existing eager Future/ExecutionContext model. No substantive actor-race discussion was found; this is an inference, not attributed historical guidance or a claim of proven exception/cancellation safety. Behavior must be tested under the chosen executor and platform.
claims.counterexample: A generic demand to replace synchronized queues, mutable state or callbacks with Cats Effect, ZIO or Ox would change the library model rather than preserve this invariant. Executor rejection and throwing hooks require separate investigation rather than assuming the normal completion path handles them.
